findings.title: Date override short-circuits before the busy check, so already-booked slots are reported available
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, once a slot falls inside a date override the function returns `true` at line 134, before the `busy.every(...)` check at the end of the function. A date override is only meant to replace the working-hours check; the host's `busy` entries (Cal bookings plus connected-calendar events) must still make the slot unavailable. Because personal events mark every user as `isFixed`, and this helper is used for both the fixed-host filter and the loose-host filter, any host with a date override will be shown as available during a time they are already booked, producing bookable slots that double-book the host. The new tests place no booking on the override day, so this is not caught.

findings.title: Working-hours check uses the slot start time for both `start` and `end`
findings.body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition only re-tests the start time and can never detect a slot that begins inside the host's working hours but ends after them (e.g. host available until 10:00, 60-minute slot at 09:30). Such slots are then accepted for fixed hosts in round-robin events, allowing a booking outside the fixed host's working hours, which is the situation this change is supposed to prevent. `end` must be derived from the slot end (`slotEndTime`), not the slot start.

findings.title: `workingHours.find` rejects a slot when any same-day range does not contain it and never rejects a non-working day
findings.body: The block rejects the slot whenever `workingHours.find(...)` returns a range whose `days` include the weekday and whose bounds do not contain the slot. This has two wrong consequences: (a) if a host has more than one availability range on the same weekday (the `Availability` model/API permits multiple rows for a date), a slot inside range 2 is still rejected because it is outside range 1; (b) if no range exists for that weekday at all (the host does not work that day), nothing matches and the slot is accepted, so a round-robin event still offers slots on days the fixed host is unavailable. The correct test is 'reject unless some range covers the slot', e.g. `workingHours.some(w => w.days.includes(day) && start >= w.startTime && end <= w.endTime)`.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on the same day: first non-matching override marks the slot unavailable
findings.body: `dateOverrides.find(...)` stops as soon as the callback returns `true`, and the callback returns `true` when the override is on the slot's day but the slot is outside that override's range. If a user has two overrides on the same date (e.g. 10:00-11:00 and 14:00-15:00, which the `Availability` table permits), a slot inside the second range is reported as unavailable because it is outside the first. The day should be classified with `some()` - is the slot covered by at least one override on that date - before deciding availability.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with `===`, so the zero-length-override check never fires
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares object references, not times, and `.add()` returns new Dayjs instances, so this is always false. The intended handling of zero-length (unavailable-day) overrides is therefore dead code, and only the following instant comparisons apply. Use `.isSame(...)` instead.

findings.title: Override day match mixes local and UTC dates and only looks at the override start
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start)` is a Dayjs in the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` was created with `.utc()`, so the `format("YYYY MM DD")` comparison compares a local date against a UTC date. On servers not running in UTC (and near day boundaries on any server) the override is attached to the wrong date. In addition, the match uses only the converted `start` instant, so an override whose real-UTC window crosses midnight (typical for early-morning overrides in positive-offset organizer timezones, e.g. 05:00-06:30 Asia/Kolkata) is not recognized for the slots after UTC midnight; those slots then fall through to the working-hours check and are wrongly dropped. Build the override window with `dayjs.utc(...)` and test whether the slot overlaps that window instead of string-comparing dates.

findings.title: No coverage for the fixed-host round-robin fix or for a booking inside a date override
findings.body: The added test only asserts the UTC output of `getSlots` for a second invitee timezone. All asserted slots (08:30-12:30 UTC) also lie inside the fixture's normal working hours (04:00-12:30 UTC), so the assertions still pass if the new date-override/working-hours logic in `checkIfIsAvailable` is removed entirely - the test does not exercise the router change. The PR's headline fix (a round-robin event whose fixed host has a date override) has no test, and no test puts an existing booking inside the override window, so the busy-check bypass in `checkIfIsAvailable` is not detected.

findings.title: Test comment gives the wrong reason for the expected result
findings.body: The comment `// it should return the same as this is the utc time` is misleading: the invitee gets the same UTC slots in both cases because the slots are absolute instants and the override is anchored to the organizer's timezone, not because 'this is the utc time'. As written it suggests the second assertion is trivially true, whereas it is precisely the assertion that fails with the old `getUTCHours()` logic (which would yield 08:00/09:00/10:00/11:00 UTC for Asia/Dhaka). The comment should explain that the override must represent the same absolute time regardless of the viewer's timezone.
